evaluation.ideal_answer: To insert a new node at the beginning of a doubly linked list, you can either create a new node with existing node references or update node references in adjacent nodes. Creating a new node is more efficient as it only requires updating the head reference and the new node's next pointer, whereas updating references in adjacent nodes would require traversing the list. For example, in a list 1 <-> 2 <-> 3, inserting a new node 0 at the beginning would result in 0 <-> 1 <-> 2 <-> 3, with the new node's next pointer referencing the old head node and the old head node's previous pointer referencing the new node.
